topic: Behavioral interview and deal experience evaluation for an Investment Banking Analyst position.

report.overall: Your communication is clear and you answer questions directly, which is great for an interview setting. However, your grammar needs more precision, particularly regarding verb tenses and subject-verb agreement, to sound more professional.
report.focusTip: Focus on using the past tense consistently when describing previous work experiences and projects.

grammar.why: The subject 'a deal' is third-person singular, so the verb needs an 's'.

grammar.quote: I see how inflation can erode
grammar.fix: I saw how inflation can erode
grammar.why: You are describing a completed observation from a past project, so the past tense is required.
The adjective 'responsible' is followed by the preposition 'for' and a gerund (-ing).
'Well' is an adverb; use the adjective 'good' to describe the noun 'result'.
You are recounting a specific past situation, so the verb should be in the past tense.

idioms.why: While 'walk through' is fine, 'take you through' sounds slightly more formal when responding to an interviewer.

idioms.upgraded: it works most of the time
idioms.why: Natives always include the definite article 'the' in this common phrase.

idioms.original: I try to show the data first
idioms.upgraded: I let the data speak for itself
idioms.why: This is a common professional idiom used when using evidence to resolve a disagreement.

transcript: I am interested because I want to understand how a deal create value. In my last project I see how inflation can erode the margin of a company very fast, so I want to work on it.
I was responsible to build the whole model in two days. The result was quite well, my manager used it in the client meeting.
When the team disagree, I try to show the data first, and then we decide together. It is not easy but it works most of time.
